identity.title: ALMA Long Baseline Campaigns: Phase Characteristics of Atmosphere at Long Baselines in the Millimeter and Submillimeter Wavelengths
identity.journal: Publications of the Astronomical Society of the Pacific

paper_type_evidence.quote: This paper presents the first detailed investigation of the characteristics of phase fluctuation and phase correction methods obtained with baseline lengths up to $\sim15$ km.

targets.name: Bright quasars observed as single source stares (e.g. 3C279, 3C454.3, 0522-364, 1924-292)

question.value: What are the atmospheric phase fluctuation characteristics at ALMA baselines up to ~15 km, how well does WVR correction work, and how well would fast switching work?

evidence.quote: we present the detailed characterization of phase fluctuation, improvement of phase fluctuation after the water vapor radiometer (WVR) phase correction method

bands.value: Bands 3, 6, 7 for all campaigns; Band 8 only in 2014

evidence.quote: We used Bands 3 (100 GHz band), 6 (200 GHz band), and 7 (300 GHz band) for all the campaigns, except for Band 8 (400 GHz band), which was only used in the 2014 campaign.

arrays.value: 12 m antennas only, ten or more per measurement

evidence.quote: We only used 12 m diameter antenna data and did not use data taken with 7 m diameter antennas
starting from the longest baseline length of 600 m in 2010 and 2011, 2 km in 2012, 3 km in 2013, and finally $10-15$ km in 2014
for tens of minutes (usually $10-40$ minutes, depending on the longest baseline length) with $\sim1$ s integration time per data point
measured between 2012 and 2014 of Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) long baseline campaigns

what.value: Typical system temperatures per ALMA band used for thermal phase noise estimate

evidence.quote: assume the source flux density is 1 Jy and the system temperature is a typical value for each ALMA Band (cite: rem15)

what.value: Site-testing radio seeing monitor 50% quartile slope 0.63 for comparison

evidence.loc: 3.2.2 Slopes for the Spatial Structure Functions
evidence.quote: consistent with the 50% quartile slope for the 3-year (1996 July – 1999 March) statistical data using the site testing 11.2 GHz radio seeing monitor of 0.63 (cite: but01)

pipeline_or_manual.value: CASA standard ALMA calibration prescription; WVR correction with wvrgcal

evidence.quote: The data were reduced using the Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA) package (cite: mcm07), using a standard ALMA calibration prescription.

smoothing.value: Data averaged to 10 s to suppress thermal noise

evidence.quote: After this, we averaged the data points for 10 s to take out phase errors due to thermal noise.

what.value: Antenna position error causing linear phase drift, details in earlier paper

evidence.quote: see (cite: fom15) for details

unstated_but_needed: Exact ALMA project codes per execution block
How SSF fit ranges and turn-over were selected per dataset
Fast-switching simulation imaging parameters and self-cal solint
Data likely requires the 2014 long baseline science verification archive data

method.value: Apply WVR correction, remove linear phase drift, average to 10 s, compute rms phase per baseline as excess path length

evidence.quote: We then calculated the rms phase fluctuation for each baseline. For the unit of phase, we express in path length.

validation.value: Thermal phase noise estimated below measured fluctuation at 15 m baselines

evidence.quote: We can therefore conclude that we successfully suppressed the effect of instrumental noise in our data with 10 s averaging.

method.value: Ratio of rms excess path length without to with WVR, averaged over baselines, vs PWV

evidence.quote: The improvement factor of the WVR phase correction method has been calculated as the ratio of the rms excess path length for each baseline without the WVR phase correction to that with the correction.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit spatial structure function slopes and constants

method.value: Fit log10(dL)=a log10(d)+b for d<500 m and d>1 km

evidence.quote: We first fitted the slopes for the data points with baseline lengths shorter than 500 m and longer than 1 km for each SSF plot

evidence.loc: 3.2.2 Slopes for the Spatial Structure Functions
evidence.quote: The fitting function is expressed as $$\begin{equation} \log_{10}(\Delta L) = a \times \log_{10}(d) + b,

validation.value: Compared with VLA and site-test slopes

evidence.loc: 3.2.2 Slopes for the Spatial Structure Functions
evidence.quote: The average slope without the WVR phase correction of $0.65\pm0.06$ is consistent with the 50% quartile slope for the 3-year (1996 July – 1999 March) statistical data using the site testing 11.2 GHz radio seeing monitor

method.value: Median coherence time at >1 km baselines for coherence 0.9, calculation stopped at 400 s

evidence.quote: Here, we calculate the coherence time that degrades the coherence to 0.9 (i.e., coherence loss of 10%).

method.value: Split 2014 stares into target, calibrator, slew; calibrate, image, compare peak flux with self-calibrated image for cycle times 28, 48, 68 s

evidence.quote: The coherence of the fast switching method is estimated by calculating the ratio of the peak flux densities between the fast switching simulation image and the self-calibrated one.

key_parameters.value: Target time 3x calibrator time, 4 s slew

evidence.quote: we used an integration time for the target of three times the integration time for the calibrator and a slew time of 4 s

assumptions.value: Target and calibrator share identical atmospheric phase

evidence.quote: since the “target” and the “calibrator” do have the same atmospheric phase fluctuation in this simulation

fitting.value: Linear fits of coherence vs cycle time

evidence.quote: We also overplotted linear fitting results of coherence as a function of cycle time as solid lines.

used_for.value: Data reduction, imaging in fast switching simulation

evidence.quote: The data were reduced using the Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA) package (cite: mcm07)
The WVR phase correction was applied using the program *wvrgcal* (cite: nik12) installed inside CASA.

results_numeric.quantity: Mean WVR improvement factor, all PWV

evidence.quote: The mean improvement factor over all PWV conditions is $2.1\pm0.7$.
with a mean improvement factor of $2.4\pm0.7$
In the case of PWV $<$ 1 mm, however, the ratio is $1.7\pm0.4$.
The average slopes are $0.22\pm0.15$ and $0.29\pm0.13$ for the data before and after the WVR phase correction
The average slopes are $0.22\pm0.15$ and $0.29\pm0.13$ for the data before and after the WVR phase correction

results_numeric.quantity: Mean rms excess path at 10 km after WVR, PWV<1 mm

evidence.quote: with a mean value of $206~\mu$m even at PWV $<$ 1 mm

results_numeric.quantity: Mean coherence time with WVR (0.9 coherence)

evidence.quote: The average of the coherence time after the WVR phase correction is 184 s, about twice longer than that without (101 s).
about twice longer than that without (101 s)

findings_qualitative.value: Most SSFs show a turn-over near 1 km, consistent with water vapor scale height; a few lack turn-over, implying a high scale-height constituent (water ice or dry component).

evidence.quote: this large scale height turbulent constituent is likely to be water ice or a dry component.

claims.hypothesis: Does WVR correction reduce phase fluctuation at long baselines?
claims.finding: WVR works well especially for PWV>1 mm

evidence.quote: The phase correction method using water vapor radiometers (WVRs) works well, especially for the cases where PWV $>1$ mm

claims.hypothesis: Is water vapor the only turbulent constituent?
claims.result: Residual fluctuation remains; some SSFs without turn-over
claims.finding: Another high scale height constituent exists

evidence.quote: phase fluctuations still remain after the WVR phase correction, suggesting the existence of other turbulent constituent

claims.result: Coherence decreases almost linearly with cycle time

evidence.quote: with shorter cycle times linearly improving the coherence

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Mountain-induced eddies, liquid water and LLC/correlator instrumental effects rejected as cause of residual phase fluctuation

evidence.quote: Since we are looking for the cause of the remaining phase fluctuation *after* successful WVR phase correction, liquid water cannot be the cause.

limitations_admitted.value: Fast switching simulation is idealized, ignoring target-calibrator separation

evidence.quote: This simulation is an idealized case

limitations_admitted.value: Coherence time underestimated due to 400 s cutoff

evidence.quote: since our calculation stops at 400 s, the coherence time is underestimated

referee_caveats_inferred: Large scatter makes PWV correlations weak
Turn-over identification is by eye with fixed ranges
Water ice/dry component attribution is speculative
